key_insight: Oxygen vacancy formation energies in binary main-group metal oxides are largely explained by cation reducibility and band gap.
engineering_relevance: Bulk-property descriptors could accelerate screening of oxide components for energy devices, although solar-cell performance was not evaluated.
method: Surveyed 39 binary oxide polymorphs using r²SCAN density functional theory.
Used ShakeNBreak to locate reconstructed neutral oxygen-vacancy ground states.
Fit an interpretable model using crystal reduction potential and band gap.
evidence_signal: Formation energies span 8 eV, and the two-descriptor model achieves a held-out mean absolute error of 0.31 eV.
watch_item: Predictions can deviate when vacancy electrons are accommodated through mechanisms beyond cation reduction; charged vacancies were not studied.
paper_title: Periodic Trends in Oxygen Vacancy Formation Energies Across Binary Main-Group Metal Oxides
